effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the errata'd text (SR06-EN036, Structure Deck: Lair of Darkness)

changes.historical_text: Activate only by paying 1000 Life Points while you have 3000 Life Points or less. Select a Normal Trap Card in your Graveyard. This card's effect is the same as that Trap Card's. Remove from play that Normal Trap Card.
changes.modern_text: If your LP is 3000 or less: Pay 1000 LP, then target 1 Normal Trap in your GY, except "Trap of Darkness"; this card's effect becomes that target's activated effect, then banish that target.
changes.summary: Functional erratum: the modern text adds 'except "Trap of Darkness"' to the copy target, so a second copy of this card sitting in the Graveyard is no longer an eligible choice; the TDGS-EN092 text said only 'Select a Normal Trap Card in your Graveyard', which admits any Normal Trap including another 'Trap of Darkness'. Everything else is PSCT: the activation condition and the 1000 LP cost are re-templated ('Activate only by paying 1000 Life Points while you have 3000 Life Points or less' -> 'If your LP is 3000 or less: Pay 1000 LP'), select becomes target with the same designation at activation, and the trailing 'Remove from play that Normal Trap Card' becomes 'then banish that target'.

gap.reason: Project Ignis ships no historical implementation of this card; reproducing the era behaviour needs a custom script and a reserved passcode
gap.behavioural_impact: In Edison the EDOPro card refuses to copy a second 'Trap of Darkness' in the Graveyard, a target the period text made legal.

review.notes: Only two English versions: v0 (TDGS-EN092, 2008-09-02), the text in force at the Edison snapshot, and v1 (SR06-EN036, 2018-04-19). Pinned BabelCDB text matches v1 exactly (ratio 1.0). upstream_implementations is empty. The self-exclusion clause is the ONLY behavioural delta I can see in the lineage; the packet carries no period ruling establishing whether the exclusion was already enforced by rulings in 2008-2010, so the verdict rests on the printed text alone, and the practical stakes are narrow (it takes a second copy of Trap of Darkness already in the Graveyard for the two texts to diverge). The card does not appear on EdisonFormat.com's functional errata page. The cost/effect split is unchanged in both readings: paying 1000 LP is an activation cost before and after.
